summary.name: Animated Line Art (Motion Design and Cinematography category). Supplemental provenance, developed from a user-requested direction. Distinct from static line art and from line boil.
summary.visualIdentity: Subjects are built from contours, connectors, arrows, and paths with consistent widths, caps, and joins. Objects are revealed before their relationships, which are then drawn, traced, or reorganized. Endpoints stay continuous, and completed structures stay readable.
summary.suitableUses: The source says the style works alone for diagrams and contour reveals. Inferred suitability: process explainers, mechanism diagrams, and step-by-step concept walkthroughs where relationships must build up in a clear order. Scene count, dimensions, and reference numbers are optional examples.
summary.limitations: The source forbids arbitrary tangled lines and endlessly repeated drawing. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Specific hand-drawn realism, pose fidelity, and asset quality limits are unspecified.
summary.palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #F9F4E7 for layout, foreground #27434A for structure, and accent_1 #AA6945 as one explanatory warm accent. Use three discrete tokens with gradients disabled. Task-supplied exact colors override these. Foreground on background measures 9.619:1, passing the 4.5 normal-text target. Accent on background measures 3.971:1, failing it, so the accent is decorative only. These are two-color checks, so composited frames must be verified.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Reveal objects first, then draw connections using stroke-dasharray, stroke-dashoffset, or DrawSVGPlugin, in explanatory order. Motion should be smooth and coherent where it helps, while deliberate cuts, reading holds, and stepped cadence are preserved. Video state derives from composition time. Live hover or scroll belongs only to interactive delivery. Motion-pattern references are optional and must match actual scene content.
summary.audio: The source sets no fixed audio requirement, so audio direction is task-specific. Inferred options include restrained background music for pacing, voiceover for explanation, or sound accents on key reveals. Silence may suit reading holds. Speech must remain intelligible without competing vocals. Specific genre, tempo, and voice are unspecified.
summary.assetRequirements: Authored line paths or exported layers are needed. Any Rough.js sketch geometry requires stable nonzero seeds and cached paths. Fonts and geometry must load before capture. tldraw may author editable diagram assets, and Paper.js may sample path points. Specific asset files, exact copy, and media are unspecified and must come from each task.
summary.combinations: Recommended hybrid one: style-001 (Swiss grid typography) for precise editorial diagrams, with labels set after their paths complete in #27434A. Recommended hybrid two: style-024 (handwritten annotations) for teaching notes added once structures are readable, using the accent. Avoid animating labels with paths, and avoid covering connectors or endpoints.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for composition, timing, validation, and export, using a paused seekable GSAP timeline. SVG is the style renderer, and DrawSVGPlugin is the motion engine, each owning distinct properties. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Verify decoded frames, audio sync, and loop seams.
